claim_text: Korea Post says hackers using overseas IP addresses broke into a mobile Internet Post Office service
summary: Korea Post says an outside hacking attack, made from overseas IP addresses, reached the mobile Internet Post Office's service for changing where registered mail is delivered.
detail: Korea Post, the national postal service, announced it on Nov 28 (Korean time). It has not said how the attackers got in.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Seoul Economic Daily: the service "came under an external hacking attack launched through overseas internet protocol addresses"; hackers "accessed a service on the mobile version of the internet post office". ZDNet Korea reports the same.

claim_text: Names, addresses and phone numbers of registered-mail recipients for Nov 17 to 24 were viewed
summary: Korea Post says the attackers viewed the names, addresses and phone numbers of customers whose registered mail was being delivered between Nov 17 and Nov 24, 2026.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Seoul Economic Daily: "Between the 17th and the 24th, they viewed the names, addresses and phone numbers of customers whose registered mail was in transit." ZDNet Korea and Yonhap (Korea Times) report the same.

claim_text: At least 113,855 people are affected, from one day's records; the other seven days are still being analysed
summary: Korea Post says one day's records alone show 113,855 customers, including companies, had their information exposed. It is still analysing the other seven days, so the total is not known.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Seoul Economic Daily: one day's data "found that 113,855 customers, including corporate accounts" had information exposed. ZDNet Korea: the other seven days are still being analysed.

claim_text: Korea Post noticed signs of the breach at about 10:30 a.m. on Nov 25 and told regulators and police
summary: Korea Post says it detected signs of the breach at about 10:30 a.m. on Nov 25 (Korean time), reported it to the Personal Information Protection Commission and asked the police to investigate.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Seoul Economic Daily: "The Korea Post detected signs of the breach at about 10:30 a.m. on the 25th. It reported the leak to the Personal Information Protection Commission and asked police to open an investigation." ZDNet Korea agrees.

claim_text: The delivery-location change service and non-member login are suspended, and overseas access to the mobile site is blocked
summary: Korea Post has temporarily suspended the delivery-location change service and the Internet Post Office's non-member login, and blocked overseas IP addresses from its mobile website. No restoration had been announced as of Nov 28.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Seoul Economic Daily: it "temporarily suspended both the delivery location change service and the non-member login service" and "blocked all overseas IP addresses". ZDNet Korea and Yonhap report the same.

claim_text: It is not yet known whether mail contents or financial information were taken, or which weakness was used
summary: ZDNet Korea reports that whether the contents of mail or financial information leaked has not yet been confirmed, and that the weakness the attackers used has not been disclosed. No one has been named as responsible.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: ZDNet Korea (in Korean): whether mail contents or financial information leaked "has not yet been confirmed, and the vulnerability used in the attack has not been disclosed either."

claim_text: Korea Post apologised and warned of texts and calls pretending to be the post office
summary: The head of Korea Post apologised and urged customers to be wary of texts or calls impersonating the post office, such as requests to change an address or pay extra delivery fees. Korea Post says it will notify affected customers.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Seoul Economic Daily: the head of Korea Post "urged customers to be cautious of suspicious text messages or calls"; Korea Post "would notify customers immediately once the damage is confirmed". ZDNet Korea reports the same.

claim_text: The breach follows other recent data breaches in South Korea, including at KEPCO
summary: Yonhap reports the Korea Post breach came amid a series of data breaches at financial institutions and public agencies in recent weeks, including a leak at the state-run Korea Electric Power Corp. involving about 1.52 million people.
detail: Nothing public links the attacks to each other.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Korea Times and Korea JoongAng Daily (both carrying Yonhap): "The latest incident came amid a series of data breaches at financial institutions and public agencies in recent weeks", including KEPCO, about 1.52 million people.

claim_text: Korea Post is South Korea's national postal service, a government agency under the Ministry of Science and ICT
summary: Korea Post is South Korea's national postal service. It is a government agency under the Ministry of Science and ICT, and also offers banking and insurance.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Wikipedia: Korea Post is a "Government statutory agency" whose parent is the Ministry of Science and ICT, with postal, banking and insurance services. Seoul Economic Daily: "an agency under the Ministry of Science and ICT".
